title: Quantum-Geometric Amplification of Nonperturbative Interaction Scales
authors: Stefano Bilamour, René Meyer, Johanna Erdmenger, Domenico Di Sante
abstract: Weak interactions at a two-dimensional quadratic band touching (QBT) can generate an exponentially small symmetry-breaking gap, $m\sim e^{-A/V_1}$, that cannot be captured by every finite order of perturbation theory. We show that the singular quantum geometry of the gapped QBT converts this beyond-all-orders scale into an algebraically enhanced response. The quantum metric develops a momentum-space hot spot whose Brillouin-zone integral diverges logarithmically, and therefore grows algebraically when the gap is dynamically generated by interactions. Through the inverse-frequency Souza--Wilkens--Martin optical sum rule, the same amplification appears in the negative-first longitudinal optical moment, even though the ordinary optical conductivity remains $O(e^2/\hbar)$ and its absorption threshold is exponentially small. We establish these results analytically for a massive QBT and verify them microscopically in an interacting kagome lattice model known to develop a spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall mass at its QBT from loop currents order. Our results identify quantum geometry as an asymptotic amplifier of nonperturbative interaction scales.
summary: This work demonstrates that quantum geometry can act as an asymptotic amplifier, converting an exponentially small, nonperturbative symmetry-breaking gap into a measurable, algebraically enhanced response. Using the kagome lattice model at a QBT, the authors show that the integrated quantum metric and optical response scale as $1/V_1$, providing a robust diagnostic tool for such weak-coupling physics.
main_problem: The paper investigates how quantum geometry can amplify nonperturbative interaction scales, converting an exponentially small symmetry-breaking gap into an algebraically enhanced response.
main_result: The exponentially small gap scale, $m \sim e^{-A/V_1}$, is converted into an algebraically large integrated geometric response, $G_{	ext{cell}} \sim 1/V_1$.
method: The analysis combines analytical derivations using continuum QBT Hamiltonians with microscopic verification using the kagome lattice model, employing variable transformations to handle exponentially small parameters.
model_or_system: The study focuses on weak interactions at a two-dimensional quadratic band touching (QBT) point, modeled using spinless fermions on the kagome lattice with repulsive nearest-neighbor interactions.
key_observables: Integrated quantum metric ($G_{	ext{cell}}$), negative-first longitudinal optical moment ($W_{	ext{tr}}^{-1}$), and the gap mass $|m_\Gamma|$.
important_parameters: Interaction strength ($V_1$), the exponentially small gap scale ($m \sim e^{-A/V_1}$), and the lattice parameters ($t, r$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the QBT structure and the assumption that the gap is generated by marginal interactions; regularization ($r>0$) is used to isolate the QBT physics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the low-energy dispersion near the QBT, the weak-coupling scaling of the interaction-generated lattice mass, and the scaling collapse of the quantum-metric trace demonstrating $1/|m_\Gamma|$ growth.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first analyzing the continuum QBT, deriving the logarithmic divergence of the quantum metric, and then applying this framework to the full kagome lattice model, culminating in the calculation of the measurable optical moment.
why_interesting: The concept of quantum geometry acting as an asymptotic amplifier provides a powerful, non-perturbative tool to extract measurable signatures from exponentially small energy scales, which is relevant for understanding exotic phases in correlated electron systems.
